newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Sampoerna won't sell Astra stake-report.
newsitem.headline: Sampoerna won't sell Astra stake-report.

text.p: Indonesian tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna, who effectively controls the single largest stake in automobile manufacturer Astra International, has denied that he will sell his holdings, Bisnis Indonesia newspaper said on Friday.
"No. I do not want to sell it," the newspaper quoted Sampoerna as saying. It said he refused to comment further.
Astra, Indonesia's largest automobile maker, has been in the news since a group linked to President Suharto said last week it was interested in buying into the company.

Muhamad "Bob" Hasan, the head of the Nusamba group, has said he is willing to buy shares in Astra from large shareholders at market prices and newspapers have said Sampoerna may be among those willing to sell.
Nusamba is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by Suharto. Hasan, a close associate of Suharto, and the president's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto own 10 percent each.

Sampoerna bought into Astra last month, setting off a steep rise in the share price. He later said he had bought 9.81 percent of the company on his own account while a subsidiary of his PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, a cigarette maker, had bought 2.85 percent.
Astra is a widely-held company and brokers have said an 18-20 percent stake may be sufficient to gain a controlling interest.
Japan's Toyota Motor Co holds an 8.26 percent stake. Astra closed at 4,050 rupiah on Thursday, up 125.
